function: Predicts beam coherence time T_B (time until beam gain falls below a threshold) so the AP updates its near-field beam only when needed, reducing overhead (p. 3).
system: THz hybrid near/far-field link: AP with 512-element ULA, single-antenna mobile UE, 142 GHz (and 280 GHz), 20 MHz; L = 2 scatterers; no RIS (pp. 2-3).
method: Feedforward network (6 fully connected layers, 12-dimensional input), supervised offline training with smooth L1 loss on labels from the numerical solver (p. 3).
data_channel: Own simulation: Gauss-Markov trajectories, spherical-wave channel with close-in path loss [13], 2.5 x 10^5 samples split 80/10/10; labels from numerical solution of (7) (pp. 3-4).
test_conditions: Trained at 142 and 280 GHz on three mobility types; tested on held-out 10% and, in Fig. 5, also at 180 and 220 GHz (pp. 3, 5).
baselines: Numerical T_B (exhaustive search, ground truth), statistical T_C updates every channel coherence time, ideal upper bound with perfect CSI and no overhead; no learned baseline (p. 4).
metrics: Effective rate in bps/Hz including beam-update overhead, average beam-update duration, inference time (pp. 3-5).
complexity: Measured average inference time 5.3 microseconds per sample versus about 2 seconds for the numerical approach with N = 512 at 142 GHz (p. 3).
q1_support: p. 4: "close-in (CI) model in [13, eq. (1)] with a path loss exponent of" - only the path gains follow a measurement-based sub-THz path loss model; the spherical-wave multipath channel with 2 random scatterers and the Gauss-Markov trajectories are a custom simulation (pp. 2-3), with no standardized model or measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "model is trained only for 142 and 280 GHz" - the effective rate in Fig. 5 is also evaluated at 180 and 220 GHz, carrier frequencies absent from the training set.
q3_support: p. 4: "closely to the ideal upper-bound, we omit other baselines and" - only non-learned references are compared (numerical T_B search, statistical T_C, ideal upper bound); no earlier learned method or standard network is included as a baseline.
q4_support: p. 3: "the measured average inference time per sample is" - 5.3 microseconds per sample for the proposed FNN, against about 2 seconds for the numerical T_B search with N = 512.
q5_support: p. 1: "relies on relevant simulated data" - the 2.5 x 10^5-sample dataset is built by the authors from their own simulation (p. 3); no code or data link or DOI is given, and no public or measured dataset is used.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match (Deep Learning Prediction of Beam Coherence Time for Near-Field TeraHertz Networks). Area 3 chosen because the learned model governs when the near-field beam is refreshed (beam tracking); the beam vector itself is computed from the UE position (p. 4), so the reviewer may prefer a function exclusion if beam-update timing is not counted as beamforming. q2 rests on the markers at 180 and 220 GHz read from Fig. 5 (p. 5), while the text only says the model is trained for 142 and 280 GHz. q1: the close-in model of [13] is a measurement-based sub-THz path loss model used only for path gains.
